finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: Marshal.load on attacker-supplied base64 data allows arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore form/query parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication

trace.note: Base64.decode64(params[:state]) passes attacker bytes directly to Marshal.load
state.inspect returned in response (also calls inspect on attacker object)

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on the payload, no class allowlist, no use of safe formats (JSON). No before filters or middleware in the file.

verdict.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load inside the unauthenticated `post "/restore"` route (app.rb:5), and app.rb is the only file, so no filter, middleware, signature or class allowlist exists.

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-6 shows POST /restore passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load with no auth, signature, or allowlist, and no other files exist in the directory, so an anonymous client can deserialize arbitrary objects.
